raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #44834.

`update_weights_from_disk` can reach the loader while weight memory is released, killing the scheduler. A release can also overtake an update waiting for the tokenizer's writer lock.

## Modifications

- Check the scheduler's `offload_tags` before invoking either weight loader. Return the existing unsuccessful response, which the HTTP handler exposes as HTTP 400, with instructions to resume weight memory.
- Keep disk updates available when only KV-cache or CUDA-graph memory is released.
- Extend the existing CPU tests with side-effect checks and a deterministic queued-update interleaving using the real tokenizer method and reader/writer lock. Extend the existing Blackwell reload test to check rejection before resuming weights.

## Accuracy Tests

Matched runs on one RTX 3050 (8 GiB), Qwen3-0.6B BF16, upstream base `3b34d9f8b6edc23216f29c1edf02d1ff0306f9de`, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.2, torch-memory-saver 0.0.10:

| Case | Baseline | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Release, then disk update | Connection dropped; scheduler died in `weight_loader` with CUDA invalid argument / allocation not found | HTTP 400 for all-region and weights-only release, with `flush_cache` both true and false |
| Update queued before release, dispatched afterward | Same scheduler failure | HTTP 400; valid reload after weight-memory resume succeeded |

The sequential baseline used the reporter's unmodified client. The GPU race check used test-only endpoints to hold the real tokenizer reader lock, observed one waiting writer from an actual disk-update HTTP request, released memory, then released the reader. No production lock behavior was changed.

After valid reloads, greedy output for the same prompt was unchanged and `/health` returned 200. Reloading while only KV memory was released also succeeded. This is lifecycle validation, not a task-accuracy evaluation.

Local checks:

- Weight-update CPU test file: **23 passed, 8 subtests passed**. The CI entry point (`python test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_weight_version_tracking.py -f`) also passed with zero visible CUDA devices. Both new rejection cases failed before the fix.
- Both added executable production lines (the guard condition and rejection return) covered; coverage started after native imports because import-time instrumentation crashed locally.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check`: passed.

Limitations: single GPU, Python radix-tree backend, prefill graphs disabled, full decode graphs enabled through batch size 32. The four-GPU Blackwell suite and live speculative/draft-model execution were not run locally; CPU coverage checks that neither target nor draft loader is invoked on rejection.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No model-forward changes. No throughput benchmark was run.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add focused regression coverage.
- [x] Follow SGLang code style.
- [ ] Run upstream GPU CI. The existing Blackwell reload suite is registered as `extra-b / 4-gpu-b200` and requires both `run-ci` and `run-ci-extra`.

AI assistance: implementation, regression tests, and the validation above were prepared with an AI coding agent.

files.patch:
@@ -137,6 +137,14 @@ def record_weight_version_after_update(self, weight_version: Optional[str]) -> N
 
     def update_weights_from_disk(self, recv_req: UpdateWeightFromDiskReqInput):
         """In-place update of the weights from disk."""
+        # A release can overtake an update waiting for the tokenizer writer lock.
+        if GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_WEIGHTS in self.offload_tags:
+            return UpdateWeightFromDiskReqOutput(
+                success=False,
+                message="Cannot update weights from disk while weight memory is released. "
+                "Call resume_memory_occupation(tags=['weights']) before updating weights.",
+                num_paused_requests=0,
+            )
         with self._observe_weight_load("disk"):
             success, message = True, "Succeeded to update model weights."
             target_updated = False

@@ -154,6 +154,14 @@ def _run_update_weights(
 
     def _offload_engine_and_resume_weights(self):
         self._post_json("/release_memory_occupation", {})
+        response = requests.post(
+            f"{self.base_url}/update_weights_from_disk",
+            json={"model_path": self.model},
+            timeout=self.update_timeout,
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 400, response.text)
+        self.assertFalse(response.json()["success"])
+        self.assertIn("resume_memory_occupation", response.json()["message"])
         self._post_json(
             "/resume_memory_occupation", {"tags": [GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_WEIGHTS]}
         )

@@ -1,17 +1,27 @@
+import asyncio
 import unittest
 from types import SimpleNamespace
-from unittest.mock import Mock, patch
+from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, Mock, patch
 
+from sglang.srt.constants import (
+    GPU_MEMORY_ALL_TYPES,
+    GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_CUDA_GRAPH,
+    GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_KV_CACHE,
+    GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_WEIGHTS,
+)
 from sglang.srt.managers.io_struct import (
     BeginWeightUpdateReqInput,
     EndWeightUpdateReqInput,
+    ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqInput,
 )
 from sglang.srt.managers.scheduler import Scheduler
 from sglang.srt.managers.scheduler_components.weight_updater import (
     SchedulerWeightUpdaterManager,
     _WeightUpdateSession,
 )
+from sglang.srt.managers.tokenizer_manager import TokenizerManager
 from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_parallel
+from sglang.srt.utils.aio_rwlock import RWLock
 from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
 from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
 
@@ -172,6 +182,102 @@ def _manager(self, target, draft=None, *, session=True):
         return manager
 
 
+class TestDiskUpdateMemoryState(_WeightUpdaterManagerTestBase):
+    def test_released_weights_reject_update_without_side_effects(self):
+        """A disk update while weights are offloaded must fail without changing either model."""
+        for tags in ({GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_WEIGHTS}, set(GPU_MEMORY_ALL_TYPES)):
+            for flush_cache in (True, False):
+                with self.subTest(tags=tags, flush_cache=flush_cache):
+                    target, draft = _runner(), _runner()
+                    manager = self._manager(target, draft)
+                    manager.offload_tags = tags.copy()
+                    manager.flush_cache = Mock(return_value=True)
+
+                    output = manager.update_weights_from_disk(
+                        _request(flush_cache=flush_cache)
+                    )
+
+                    self.assertFalse(output.success)
+                    self.assertIn("resume_memory_occupation", output.message)
+                    self.assertEqual(output.num_paused_requests, 0)
+                    target.weight_updater.update_weights_from_disk.assert_not_called()
+                    draft.weight_updater.update_weights_from_disk.assert_not_called()
+                    manager.flush_cache.assert_not_called()
+                    self.assertEqual(self.recorded, [])
+                    self.assertEqual(manager.offload_tags, tags)
+
+    def test_other_released_regions_allow_disk_update(self):
+        """RL may reload weights before resuming the KV cache and CUDA graphs."""
+        for tags in (
+            set(),
+            {GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_KV_CACHE},
+            {GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_CUDA_GRAPH},
+            {GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_KV_CACHE, GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_CUDA_GRAPH},
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(tags=tags):
+                self.recorded.clear()
+                manager = self._manager(_runner())
+                manager.offload_tags = tags.copy()
+
+                output = manager.update_weights_from_disk(_request())
+
+                self.assertTrue(output.success)
+                self.assertEqual(self.recorded, ["v2"])
+                self.assertEqual(manager.offload_tags, tags)
+
+    def test_queued_update_is_rejected_after_memory_release(self):
+        """A release can overtake an update waiting for the generation reader lock."""
+        target = _runner()
+        manager = self._manager(target)
+        manager.memory_saver_adapter = Mock()
+        manager.scheduler._engine_paused = False
+
+        async def run():
+            async def dispatch(request):
+                output = manager.update_weights_from_disk(request)
+                return output.success, output.message, output.num_paused_requests
+
+            tokenizer = SimpleNamespace(
+                auto_create_handle_loop=Mock(),
+                is_pause_cond=asyncio.Condition(),
+                is_pause=False,
+                model_update_lock=RWLock(),
+                mm_processor=None,
+                _wait_for_model_update_from_disk=AsyncMock(side_effect=dispatch),
+            )
+            request = _request(
+                load_format="safetensors", abort_all_requests=False, weight_version=None
+            )
+            async with tokenizer.model_update_lock.reader_lock:
+                update = asyncio.create_task(
+                    TokenizerManager.update_weights_from_disk(tokenizer, request)
+                )
+                await asyncio.sleep(0)
+                self.assertFalse(update.done())
+                self.assertEqual(tokenizer.model_update_lock._waiting_writers, 1)
+                tokenizer._wait_for_model_update_from_disk.assert_not_awaited()
+                manager.release_memory_occupation(
+                    ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqInput(tags=[GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_WEIGHTS])
+                )
+
+            success, message, _ = await asyncio.wait_for(update, timeout=5)
+            self.assertFalse(success)
+            self.assertIn("resume_memory_occupation", message)
+            target.weight_updater.update_weights_from_disk.assert_not_called()
+            self.assertEqual(self.recorded, [])
+
+        module = "sglang.srt.managers.scheduler_components.weight_updater"
+        with (
+            patch(f"{module}._export_static_state", return_value={}),
+            patch(
+                f"{module}.get_model",
+                return_value=SimpleNamespace(weight_cache_mode="off"),
+            ),
+            patch("torch.get_device_module"),
+        ):
+            asyncio.run(run())
+
+
 class TestRecordWeightVersionAfterUpdate(_WeightUpdaterManagerTestBase):
     def test_successful_update_records_the_version(self):
         """A refit that reports success advances the scheduler-side version."""
